en: Drawing breath like a dragon,
The beastly world rises in enmity.
The encampment of everyone he encountered,
I shall be Chyng Temir.
The eighteen thousand worlds,
If he gathered and seized them wholesale,
I shall drive them on and exact tribute.
If my fury rises and I strike with a curse,
Would the black mountain not be shattered?
If a stark command comes from the khan,
Would its onslaught not find them?
When the Mongols stood in Beijing,
Would he not exact tribute from a whole world?
If you stiffen in anger,
The four corners of the world,
The five quarters you have marked out,
Would they not be smashed to pieces?
When I become Chyng Temir,
Scorching until the sands were swept up,
When rejoicing, he was no mere common man,
The valleys shook and mountains fell,
My valiant one knew it.
As the age approached its end,
Thus he came to Kakan,
Saying the enemy would not take what was given,
He was destined for great dominion.
Saying this, Chyng Temir,
Angrily gathered an army,
When he gathered troops, he gathered a multitude,
Those younger than fifty-five,
Let not a single old soul remain,
Those who had passed eighteen,
The roll of the young men,
Saying not one youth should remain behind,
Kakan, root and branch,
He gathered them all together.
From the elder side came grievous slaughter.
He had cast the people into a dispute.
Their wits bewildered, their heads aching,
He had cast the people into turmoil,
He did not stand by and watch in vain,
An extraordinary upheaval, a great conflict,
The people were ruined and the nation grieved,
An extraordinary affliction, a great conflict,
The people rose and began to assemble.
Of what the Kalmyk had given,
Of what had long been increasing since ancient times,
The Kyrgyz asked grimly.
A wrathful scourge began.
The people cried out and tumult arose,
When they looked, nothing caught the eye,
The people stirred in a great upheaval,
Its sorrow could not be discerned,
They gathered an army for the contest,
They gathered the whole host in great numbers.
Together they stood in Kongol,
The affliction that threw the people into panic,
How the True Lord had measured it,
Such was the command he gave.
The great Chinese nation cried aloud,
They had witnessed their khan’s wrath,
Stricken by its warrior,
The brave Eren, Khan Esen,
Sat burdened with worry,
While the people cried out in distress,
As he was about to take up his decree,
His wrath became known to the people,
A merciless ordeal began,
Even their livestock were plundered,
All the people found no refuge,
Asking what this khan’s decree might be,
The populace cowered in fear,
The wise among them marveled,
The witless did not understand,
Bewildered by milk and kumis,
The people stood pale with longing.
Chyng Tengir was indeed a mighty lord,
Kakanchy and Beijing were his support,
Not merely Beijing, but the whole world—
The time had come for him to rule it,
A true mainstay of the world,
The time had come for him to become one.
A sage, accomplished in stratagems,
Even the black scourge could not escape
Those who knew the extent of their cunning,
From the inspector who roamed the land,
From the dark eye of calamity,
From the dark eye of the scourge,
With doors open and belts loosened,
The dear people living at ease,
Making them move as though within a bend,
The affairs of the great host were secret,
Yet he had learned them all,
The command that Chaan had carried out,
When that troubled time arose among the people,
My elder Etек acted,
And learned its immense secret.
With a name of bitter wrath,
He had arrived at that place.
To the son of Heaven,
He related it without holding back.
Not leaving out a single word,
He told the truth.
Of the lineage of the Black Kyrgyz,
He disclosed its secret.
One could not bear to see another,
One would not heed another’s word,
Now of those people and that nation,
He disclosed the secret.
Of the small force that knew how to destroy,
He told the truth.
Of the camp of the warrior Esen,
Börköy gave an account,
Of his many clamoring people,
He gave a full account.
The horse he rode was a bay thoroughbred,
He was a man of fierce courage,
Called the hero Kulan Saryk,
He had two sons.
The younger and elder brothers lacked unity,
Such were those people.
To the warrior Esen concerning this,
He was a man regarded as a warrior.
Saying this, Chañ Buzer continued,
To the sovereign of Heaven,
He related everything.
From the Amroolu Kyrgyz,
He brought and delivered the report.
Of the small Amroolu people,
He turned their grievance into conflict,
Coming into the fire and making a secret pact,
If they falter, we shall demand and take it,
If they seize a single soul on the plain,
We shall bring down their young and seize them.
The unruly Kyrgyz lineage,
We shall drive them on and exact tribute.
If by chance they strike the frontier,
We shall fight them in the Kyrgyz manner.
Closely surrounding them on four sides,
We shall shout and cast terror upon them,
On the dire day when they are hemmed in,
Warrior, we shall take the fourfold blood-price.
With neither complaint nor quarrel,
With neither guile nor hidden secret,
Without the least corrupt dispute,
We shall take the realm of forty khans.
If they rage and fight,
If they scatter and fight,
We shall spill their wrathful blood.
We shall advance under cover,
Without delay, we shall open their eyes.
Ala-Too is no land cheaply won,
If one should assail it by chance,
Those Kyrgyz are no easy people.
All twelve months, in fair weather and winter,
You take the moon’s breeze,
When the people set out for the uplands,
In the season when the horse’s tongue turns black,
When the riverbed fills with water,
When the nightingale alights upon the tree,
When the cuckoo calls at dawn,
When roe deer cry from mountain to mountain,
When the snow breaks loose from Mongul,
When the river surges and the waters swell,
When embers from the khan fill the land,
Then livestock and people take courage.
When strength enters him as he bends,
Guests will not remain on the uplands,
When the time comes to camp on the khan’s summer pasture,
How much shall I see again?
I will divide his people, leaving none behind.
I will slaughter those of his paradise,
Let it be restored after one lord has died.
After his treasury has perished,
I will scatter his abundant wealth,
If they rebel, we number thousands.
The fleet breed of the Kyrgyz,
We will strike one of their petty lords.
If we rise stiffly in wrath,
True Tengir will strike as he has said,
We will unleash a single great tumult.
The wrathful one’s people are far away,
We will plunder them, leaving nothing,
We will hand over his paradise,
You saw the paradise of those people,
We will burn their champions,
Their brave men and lions,
We will drive and gather them in the valley,
I will make it an utter scourge,
I will bring disaster upon their heads,
Destroying all their people,
I will be sated with one haul of booty.
Not merely six enemies, but a hundred enemies,
If it stands, its world is an arrow.
Hero, when his savage frenzy seizes him,
One man’s demon is his wrath.
That one is of the Kyrgyz stock,
Let us find one oppressor.
Calamity and affliction,
We will set them upon head after head,
The chief design of the Manghit,
If we charge in, we will seize it.
Kakansan grew wrathful,
We shall bring slaughter upon China.
Such was the testament that was made,
This is what the ear heard.
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
There is the Heaven-khan in Beijing.
Kakansan grew wrathful,
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
Go and declare your grievance before them.
You have many words already spoken,
In Chañu, which was laid waste,
At the corner where corrupt words were uttered,
You have a name that can bring ruin.
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
If you grow wrathful, you will prevail,
If you refuse the words that are spoken,
If they will not walk the road appointed,
The great people of Beijing,
When the warrior speaks in anger,
If you lash the world onward,
Look upon it and act,
You have put it to the test; know this.
Take the word of Heaven from abroad,
He gained the land without making a raid,
He took the people who had been overrun,
The nation’s inherited wealth is a tethering stake,
Heroism requires a people,
To range abroad requires land.
The people are dear, the nation is a pledge,
What the ear has heard and the eye has seen,
We shall divide it as an inheritance for the people.
Kakansan grew wrathful,
All of the wide world,
You will see gathered together.
Saying this, Zhan Zhetpes continued,
Saying that he had become a sovereign in peace.
One from each and every people,
Saying, “Appoint one from among the envoys,”
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
Saying, “Let Chyng Temir be the padishah,”
Send an envoy between us,
Without clashing or quarreling,
Take counsel and testimony from the people.
If you clash and quarrel,
His valor is not greater than the people’s,
Your thunder is not so great,
Do not turn this into a reckless affair,
What I have said to you is no great thing.
Bow to one who bows,
He is one of a heroic people,
They are a people who know cultivation,
My lord, his road and passage are open,
He is one of a heroic people.
From one who stands as a shield for the people,
